summary: Verified the lock preview safety path in src/main.rs and the related tests: left click exits through request_state/exit_lockscreen, keyboard mode is None, the PowerButton arm never spawns swaylock, and lock materials are dropped. Supplied screenshot plus source-rendered Quicksand metrics confirm the clock is rendered faithfully to its source font, but that font's visible glyph metrics remain measurably narrower and lighter than the reference after controlling digit identity; the current width test pins advances, not ink.

findings.title: Lock clock ink metrics still miss the reference and the test masks it
findings.detail: Reference '11:28' bright-ink bbox is 868x279 (ink/cap 3.112). Rendering the same string with the vendored Quicksand-Bold at 0.27*1440 gives 821x277 (ink/cap 2.964), about 5% narrow; reference colon dots are ~81x81 versus source/current ~52x52 native, ~36-55% smaller. The current '17:06' screenshot is 942x292 native and matches its source raster 944x294, so this is not screenshot scaling or digit identity. lockscreen_layout and clock_block_uses_proportional_advances use the sum of font advances as clock_block.w (~3.10/cap) and compare that to the reference's ink/cap 3.122, so the test passes while visible ink does not match. Keep CLOCK_PX_FRAC/cap height as-is; match the rasterized ink geometry (font/weight or optical glyph correction) and test actual glyph coverage.

what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a rasterized-ink assertion for '11:28' at 1440p (bbox roughly 868x279, colon dots roughly 81px) and make the lock glyph source meet it without shrinking cap height, while preserving the verified click-exit/no-grab/no-locker path.
